title: refgenie: registry genome YAML, RefgetStore build table, refgenie 1.x server API records, legacy refgenie 0.x genome_config
maintainer: Sheffield lab, University of Virginia (refgenie project, github.com/refgenie)

formats.description: One genome entry of the refgenie-registry (genomes/<organism>/<name>.yaml), validated by schema/genome.schema.yaml. Each entry is one named sequence collection (one exact set of sequences, pinned by seqcol.digest) plus organism, assembly accession, FASTA download URLs, optional FHR provenance, and registry build instructions.
formats.record_key: name (unique in the registry; equals the file stem); seqcol.digest when present

formats.description: RefgetStore build table (refgenie-registry stores/<store>/sources.csv), validated by stores/sources_schema.json. One row per FASTA (or space-separated FASTAs concatenated) to load into a store; each row becomes one sequence collection. Columns beyond the schema's are allowed and differ by store.
formats.record_key: fasta (the PEP sample_table_index of most stores; unique within one store)

formats.description: refgenie 1.x server genome record, GET https://api.refgenie.org/v4/genomes/{digest} (OpenAPI schema GenomeDetailResponse). The genome DB columns (refgenie/db/tables.py GenomePublic) plus the species row and the genome's FHR sidecar under 'fhr'.

refgenie 1.x server genome listing, GET https://api.refgenie.org/v4/genomes?alias=... (OpenAPI schema PageResponse[GenomeResponse]). One record per genome in 'results'; unlike the detail record it lists every alias of the genome and an asset count, but has no FHR block.

refgenie 1.x server alias resolution, GET https://api.refgenie.org/v4/aliases/{name} (OpenAPI schema AliasResponse): the alias, its genome digest, the seqcol level-2 arrays (names, lengths, sequences) and the FHR sidecar.

refgenie 1.x server sequence table, GET https://api.refgenie.org/v4/genomes/{digest}/sequences (OpenAPI schema GenomeSequencesResponse). The adapter gives one record per element of 'sequences'; row fields use their own names (name, length, ...) and the collection fields (digest, n_sequences, total_length, level1.*, collection_aliases) are repeated on every row.

Legacy refgenie 0.x genome configuration file (genome_config.yaml, config_version 0.4), read by refgenconf and by Galaxy's 'refgenie' tool data table type. Also accepts the bare 'genomes' block that refgenieserver 0.x serves at /_private_api/genomes/dict. The adapter gives one record per genome/asset/tag; map keys (genome digest, asset name, tag name) appear as {genome}, {asset}, {tag} placeholders in the paths.

fields.description: Primary identifier of this registry genome (e.g. hg38, R64-1-1). Must equal the YAML file stem. Exported to FHR 'genome'.
fields.notes: Pattern ^[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]+$. Names one exact sequence collection, not an assembly: hg38 here is the NCBI no-alt analysis set with UCSC names. Registered as a refgenie alias; a store row for this genome must use exactly this string as its 'name'. Unique within the registry.

fields.description: Other names for this genome (e.g. GRCh38 for hg38). Exported to FHR 'genomeSynonym' and registered as refgenie aliases of the collection digest.
fields.notes: Each alias resolves to one digest in refgenie's alias namespace. May not contain '/'. Mixes assembly names (GRCh38) with provider labels (sacCer3-igenomes-ucsc); 'GRCh38' here means this one collection, not the assembly. Duplicates occur in some files (hg38_p14_genomic lists the same alias twice).

fields.description: Human-readable description of this genome. Exported to FHR 'documentation' unless fhr.documentation overrides.
fields.example:
GRCh38 (hg38) no-alt analysis set from NCBI (GCA_000001405.15): primary
chromosomes, unplaced and unlocalized scaffolds, chrM and chrEBV, with no ALT
haplotypes; UCSC-style names (chr1, chrM).
fields.notes: Free text, often a YAML block scalar with line breaks and a trailing newline. Often states naming style and which sequences are included.

fields.description: Binomial species name (e.g. Homo sapiens). Exported to FHR taxon.name.
NCBI Taxonomy ID (e.g. 9606). Exported as FHR taxon.uri https://identifiers.org/taxonomy:{taxon_id}.
fields.notes: Species-level taxon in practice (yeast uses 4932, not the S288C strain taxon 559292).

fields.description: Authoritative source of this assembly per the schema (e.g. NCBI, Ensembl, UCSC, Gencode, Broad). Exported as the FHR extension 'assemblySource' and the refgenie 'assembly_source' column.
fields.notes: Despite the name, values say who produced this packaging/naming of the sequences, not who assembled the genome: sacCer3 says UCSC and R64-1-1 says Ensembl for the same S288C assembly. Case is not normalized across sources (registry 'NCBI', some store rows 'ncbi').

fields.description: Assembly accession (e.g. GCA_000001405.15, GCF_000001405.40). Exported to FHR accessionID; its version number becomes FHR 'version'.
fields.notes: Identifies the assembly globally, but several registry genomes share one accession (hg38, hg38_full_analysis and hg38_full_analysis_plus_decoy all cite GCA_000001405.15), so it does not identify a record. Many other GRCh38 collections (Ensembl, GENCODE, Broad flavors) set no accession at all. GCA vs GCF prefix is meaningful (GenBank vs RefSeq). Absent for UCSC-only entries such as sacCer3.

fields.description: Assembly level: chromosome, scaffold or contig. Exported as FHR extension 'assemblyLevel'.
fields.notes: Enum [chromosome, scaffold, contig].

fields.description: Masking applied: soft-masked, hard-masked, not-masked or unknown. Exported to FHR 'masking'.
fields.notes: Not set in any record collected on 2026-11-17, so no example. Soft-masking (lowercase) does not change refget/seqcol digests, which uppercase sequences, so it is a property of the file; hard-masking (N) does change the sequences and so the collection.

fields.description: Name of the provider of each FASTA download (e.g. NCBI, UCSC, Ensembl, Gencode, Broad, iGenomes).
fields.notes: Parallel to fasta.sources[].url; None where a source has no provider. Registry-only, not exported to FHR.

fields.description: Download URL of each FASTA file for this genome (http, https or ftp).
fields.notes: Parallel to fasta.sources[].provider. Several URLs are alternative copies of the same content (assumed, not checked here). Usually gzipped. These are upstream URLs; the store's own staged path is in the sources.csv 'fasta' column and is a different string. Registry-only, not exported to FHR.

fields.description: SHA-256 of the uncompressed FASTA file, or the sentinel 'compute_on_registration'. Exported as FHR checksum 'sha256:{hash}' unless the sentinel.
fields.notes: Every genome YAML in the registry on 2026-11-17 uses the sentinel; no real hash is recorded. Which of several fasta.sources it refers to is not stated.

fields.description: MD5 of the compressed FASTA file (32 lowercase hex).
fields.notes: Of the compressed (.gz) file, unlike sha256 which is of the uncompressed file. Registry-only, not exported to FHR.

fields.description: GA4GH sequence collection top-level digest (32-char base64url). The canonical genome identifier, the refgenie genome digest, and the .fhr.json sidecar filename.
fields.notes: Required unless seqcol.compute is true. Same value as the refgenie 1.x API 'digest'. Different from the legacy refgenie 0.x genome digest (48 hex chars).

fields.description: Number of sequences in the collection.
fields.notes: Registry-only, not exported to FHR.

fields.description: If true, the registry computes the seqcol digest at registration (used instead of seqcol.digest).
fields.notes: Registry pipeline instruction.

fields.description: SPDX license identifier for the assembly data (schema example CC0-1.0). Exported to FHR 'license'.
fields.notes: Not set in any record collected on 2026-11-17, so no example. gtars extension; upstream FHR uses reuseConditions.

fields.description: Funding line item. Exported to FHR 'funding'.
fields.notes: Not set in any record collected on 2026-11-17, so no example.

fields.description: DOI of the article publishing the assembly. Exported to FHR 'scholarlyArticle'.
fields.notes: Not set in any record collected on 2026-11-17, so no example.

fields.description: Assembly creation date (ISO 8601). Exported to FHR 'dateCreated'.
fields.notes: Set mostly on VGP genomes (26 of ~709 YAMLs). The adapter returns it as an ISO string even when the YAML has an unquoted date.

fields.description: Description of the physical sample. Exported to FHR 'voucherSpecimen'.
fields.notes: Not set in any record collected on 2026-11-17, so no example.

fields.notes: Registry pipeline instruction, never exported to FHR. The same collection can also sit in other stores (hg38 says 'legacy' but api.refgenie.org serves it from 'jungle').

fields.description: How far the registry builds this genome: store_only, sequence_only, standard or full (each includes the tiers below).
fields.notes: Registry pipeline instruction.

fields.description: Extra refgenie assets (recipe names) to build beyond the tier.
fields.notes: Registry pipeline instruction.

fields.description: Assets (recipe names) to skip from the tier.
fields.notes: Registry pipeline instruction.

fields.notes: Registry bookkeeping; returned as an ISO string.

fields.description: GitHub username of the contributor.
fields.notes: Registry bookkeeping.

fields.description: Date the FASTA URL and checksum were last verified.
fields.notes: Registry bookkeeping; set on only 2 YAMLs.

fields.description: Path or URL of the FASTA file to load. Relative paths resolve against the store's fasta_root (project_config.yaml). Several space-separated URLs are downloaded and concatenated into one collection.
fields.notes: URL (http/https/ftp/s3) or path. The string the store ingests, often a staged local path, so it differs from the upstream URL in the genome YAML. Unique within one store (PEP sample_table_index).

fields.description: Short human-readable identifier for this collection; registered as a refgenie alias.
fields.notes: When a genome YAML exists for the row, must equal the YAML 'name'. May repeat across rows only if all those rows load the same collection (otherwise it is not registered). No '/'.

fields.description: Binomial species name.
fields.notes: Not always a plain binomial: plantcore uses 'Saccharomyces cerevisiae strain S288C'. Looked up in tools/taxon_ids.json to get the taxon id for FHR.

fields.description: Authority or provider that produced this FASTA (e.g. GENCODE, Ensembl, NCBI, UCSC, VGP, HPRC).
fields.notes: Case and wording are not normalized: 'ensembl' and 'Ensembl', 'ncbi' and 'NCBI', 'NCBI RefSeq', 'broad', 'refgenie'. Exported as FHR assemblySource for rows without a genome YAML.

fields.description: Release or version identifier assigned by the provider (GENCODE '49', Ensembl '115', RefSeq 'GRCh38.p13').
fields.notes: Only the salmon_txomes store uses it among the stores collected.

fields.description: The genome assembly this collection is based on (e.g. GRCh38, GRCm39, T2T-CHM13v2.0); for transcriptomes, the assembly the transcripts come from.
fields.notes: Values mix assembly names (GRCh38, R64-1-1) with UCSC build names (hg38, sacCer3), iGenomes build folders (build3.1 is labeled R64-1-1, GRCh38Decoy) and provider release labels (ENSEMBL_release_81). Also registered as a collection alias under the 'genome_assembly' namespace when all rows with that value are the same collection.

fields.description: INSDC/RefSeq assembly accession (GCA_ or GCF_).
fields.notes: A claim: build_aliases.py registers it as an insdc/refseq alias only if the collection's content matches NCBI's assembly report. Empty for most analysis sets and repackaged copies.

fields.description: Other names that search should find but that are not aliases, separated by ';'. Published as FHR genomeSynonym for rows with no genome YAML.
fields.notes: One string, not a list. Example: the iGenomes path Saccharomyces_cerevisiae/UCSC/sacCer3.

fields.description: Categorical label for organizing collections within a store (e.g. vertebrates, homo_sapiens, assembly, transcript).
fields.notes: Free label; meaning varies by store (species folder in jungle, sequence type in vrs).

fields.description: Store-specific extra column (jungle, plantcore, plantsup): the sample name in the original PEP the row came from.
fields.notes: Not in sources_schema.json properties; allowed by additionalProperties. Often the row's former name.

fields.description: Store-specific extra column (salmon_txomes): URL of the matching GTF annotation file.
fields.notes: A different file (annotation), not the FASTA.

fields.description: Store-specific extra column (salmon_txomes): per sources_schema.json, a 'legacy Salmon index hash'.
fields.notes: Not a checksum of the FASTA in 'fasta'. Unsure exactly what was hashed (likely the tximeta/Salmon index signature); do not map it to a file checksum.

fields.description: Store-specific extra column (vrs): URL of the NCBI assembly report for the accession.
fields.notes: Assembly-level document used to name sequences and prove accessions.

fields.description: Store-specific extra column (pangenome): population label of the HPRC sample.
fields.notes: Describes the sampled individual.

fields.description: Genome digest: the GA4GH seqcol top-level digest (32 chars). Primary key of the genome table.
fields.notes: Same as registry seqcol.digest. Not the legacy 0.x 48-hex digest.

fields.description: Genome description (from FHR documentation).

fields.description: Namespace of each RefgetStore collection alias.
fields.notes: Parallel to collection_aliases[].alias. Seen: 'name' (sources.csv name / YAML aliases), 'genome_assembly' (sources.csv genome_assembly). The README also describes 'insdc' and 'refseq' assembly aliases.

fields.description: Each collection alias in the store holding this genome.
fields.notes: Unique within its namespace. Only aliases from the one serving store, so fewer than the server's full alias list.

fields.description: Sequence name (FASTA ID) within this collection.
fields.notes: Row field. Unique within the collection only. Naming style differs between collections of the same assembly (chrI vs I, chrM vs Mito).

fields.description: Sequence length in bases.
fields.notes: Row field.

fields.description: GA4GH refget sequence digest (truncated SHA-512, base64url), without the 'SQ.' prefix.
fields.notes: Row field. Same sequence, same digest, whatever its name.

fields.description: MD5 of the uppercased sequence (refget md5).
fields.notes: Row field. Nullable per the OpenAPI schema; every row collected has one.

fields.description: RefgetStore storage alphabet chosen for this sequence: dna2bit (ACGT), dna3bit, dnaio (IUPAC), protein or ASCII.
fields.notes: Row field. A storage detail of the store, not a property of the biology.

fields.description: Rest of the FASTA header line after the ID.
fields.example: AC:CM000663.2  gi:568336023  LN:248956422  rl:Chromosome  M5:6aef897c3d6ff0c78aff06ac189178dd  AS:GRCh38
fields.notes: Row field. Not a refgenie field: raw defline text. In the NCBI analysis set it carries tags: AC (INSDC accession), rl (role: Chromosome, unlocalized, unplaced, Mitochondrion, decoy), rg (parent chromosome), M5 (md5), AS (assembly), tp (topology). Null when the header has no description.

fields.description: Namespace of each sequence alias (seen: refseq, insdc).
fields.notes: Row field, parallel to aliases[].alias. Empty lists when no aliases are proven (all yeast rows).

fields.description: Each sequence alias, e.g. NC_000001.11 (refseq), CM000663.2 (insdc).
fields.notes: Row field. Registered only when build_aliases.py proves it (ENA md5 match, NCBI '=' identity, or name+length).

fields.description: Config file format version (0.4 for refgenie >= 0.10).
fields.notes: Top-level; repeated on every record. Absent in the bare genomes block served by refgenieserver.

fields.description: Parent folder of refgenie-managed assets on this machine.
fields.notes: Top-level; repeated on every record.

fields.description: URLs of refgenieserver instances to pull from.
fields.notes: Top-level.

fields.description: Single server URL used by config versions before 0.4 (CFG_SERVER_KEY).
fields.notes: Not set in any record collected on 2026-11-17, so no example.

fields.description: refgenieserver setting: named remote locations ({name: {prefix, description}}) whose prefixes build archive download URLs.
fields.notes: Top-level object kept whole. Not in refgenconf's CFG_TOP_LEVEL_KEYS; written by refgenieserver deployments.

fields.description: Folder where refgenieserver stores asset archives.
fields.notes: Top-level.

fields.description: Path of the archive config file (relative to the archive folder).
fields.notes: Top-level.

fields.description: URL prefix for served asset archives when they are not local.
fields.notes: Not set in any record collected on 2026-11-17, so no example.

fields.description: Map key of one genome: in config 0.4 the legacy refgenie genome digest (48 hex chars); in 0.3 and earlier, the genome name.
fields.notes: Legacy digest (refgenconf/seqcol.py fasta_seqcol_digest) = truncated SHA-512 (first 24 bytes, hex) of the comma-joined item digests, where each item digest hashes (FASTA header line, length, sequence digest) for one sequence, in file order. Not the GA4GH seqcol digest: hg38 is 2230c535... here and EiFob05a... in refgenie 1.x. The FASTA header used is the whole line, description included, and sequences are not uppercased.

fields.description: Human-readable names for this genome (e.g. hg38).
fields.notes: Galaxy's refgenie tool data table uses the first alias as dbkey (rgc.get_genome_alias with fallback to the digest).

fields.description: Description of the genome.
fields.notes: Galaxy shows it in the display name: '<description> (refgenie: <alias>@<asset digest>)'.

fields.description: Genome digest attribute used in config 0.3 when genomes were keyed by name (CFG_CHECKSUM_KEY).
fields.notes: Not set in any record collected on 2026-11-17, so no example.

fields.description: Map key: asset name (e.g. fasta, bwa_index, bowtie2_index, star_index).
fields.notes: Unique within a genome. Galaxy selects genomes by asset name (table asset='fasta').

fields.description: Description of what the asset contains and how it was built.
fields.example: DNA sequences in the FASTA format, indexed FASTA (produced with samtools index) and chromosome sizes file
fields.notes: Describes the asset type, not the genome.

fields.description: Tag used when none is given.
Map key: tag name (usually 'default').
fields.notes: Unique within an asset.

fields.description: Path of the asset folder, relative to the genome folder (or absolute).
Digest of the asset directory contents (32 hex), used for provenance on pull and build.
fields.notes: Galaxy puts it in the entry value: refgenie:{alias}/{asset}:{tag}@{asset_digest}.

fields.description: Map of seek key name to file path inside the asset folder.
fields.notes: Kept whole because the keys depend on the asset. For the fasta asset: fasta (the .fa file), fai, chrom_sizes, dir. Paths are relative to asset_path.

fields.description: Assets used to build this one, as 'digest/asset:tag'.
fields.notes: Provenance links.

fields.description: Assets built from this one, as 'digest/asset:tag'.
fields.notes: Provenance links.

fields.description: Checksum of the asset archive (.tgz) served by refgenieserver (32 hex).
fields.notes: Server archive config only.

fields.description: Archive digest under an older archiving scheme.
fields.notes: Not in refgenconf constants; written by refgenieserver archive tooling. Unsure of the exact algorithm.

fields.description: Human-readable size of the unpacked asset (e.g. '2.9GB').
fields.notes: String with unit, not a number.

fields.description: Human-readable size of the archive (e.g. '833.4MB').
fields.notes: String with unit, not a number.
